why_this_rate: The rate every section here was read and scored at: the unit's output ends between sixteen and eighteen kilohertz, and a chain at thirty-two ends there.

map.why: Two states and the boundary is between 0 and 1: one value of the byte selects one corner and the other 127 select the other. The figure is the half point of the deviation, which is where this model's corner parameter is defined.
The byte answers over a window of twenty-five values centred on 64 and sticks at both ends. Read at every value between 48 and 80: 52 and below return the same cut and 76 and above the same boost.

The named third octaves between the printed ends, indexed by the byte's top four bits. Read off the page and the era rather than off these takes: the fitted positions this model used to carry sit up to a sixth of an octave below the table at the bottom of the range, which is a curve fitted over a peak two octaves wide being pulled towards its longer flank. At the narrowest width the unit's peak stands in the band the table names. One entry of the sixteen is not the series: the third sits at 279.1 Hz where the named third octave is 315.0, on both mid addresses of this type and on the mid section of two combination types. The frequency class publishes that figure as a readout beside its claim and holds the entry open, and this candidate carries it. Fifteen entries here could have come out wrong and one could not, which is why the candidate without it is ranked beside this one rather than replaced by it.

The five figures the page prints, halved. Scored against every band profile of this type whose swept address is a mid width byte: the printed figures give seven times the residual and lean on two of the three records that carry a feature, and the halved list leans on none. Nothing in it was fitted.

what_is_not_modelled: A peaking cut that is not its boost mirrored: measured on one section, bounded to a quarter of a decibel over most of the byte, and absent from every model here.
what_varies: Every section built at the gain its byte names, which is what the chain was scored as before either gain-path claim was read.
